title: Adaptive burst threshold tuner and KV preemption policy for high-QPS workloads
creator: Amara Patel
description:
Problem: Under sustained high QPS with many short sequences we see frequent microbursting that drives GPU memory saturation and causes tail-latency regressions. Existing admission heuristics are brittle: either they apply blunt drop policies or they wait until eviction pressure causes quality regressions.

Objective: Implement an adaptive burst-threshold tuner that continuously learns per-model/per-slot burst tolerances and applies graded backpressure, combined with a KV preemption policy that prioritizes evicting cache entries with low predicted reuse instead of naive LRU. The goal is to reduce 95th/99th percentile latencies by 20% and decrease out-of-memory evictions by 30% on high-QPS customer workloads, without increasing token-cost for steady-state traffic.

Approach summary:
- Burst threshold tuner: use an online percentile estimator (P99 of cumulative slot occupancy over sliding window) to set soft micro-batch admission thresholds per-GPU and per-model. Thresholds adapt across hours and correlate with sequence-length distribution.
- Graded backpressure: on exceeding soft threshold, introduce token-level hold delays (10-200ms) with exponential backoff rather than immediate rejection; escalate to admission shedding only if delays exceed configured SLOs.
- KV preemption policy: implement a weighted preemption score = alpha * (1 - reuse_prob) + beta * size_factor + gamma * recency_factor. Reuse_prob is estimated using a lightweight Bloom-filter based sampler and short-term reuse counters that predict near-future hits.
- GPU memory optimizer: partition GPU cache slab into priority bands (hot/warm/cold). Preempt cold band aggressively under pressure; allow hot-band pinned entries for in-flight contexts. Implement a fast path for small common prefixes to stay resident.
- Safety/rollback: feature gated behind runtime flag; metrics and canary rollout to 10% of GPUs, revert if OOM or quality regressions observed.

Why this is different: rather than static thresholds or pure LRU eviction, this design combines predictive reuse estimation with soft, latency-aware backpressure so the system trades a few ms of delay to avoid expensive evictions and GPU stalls.
acceptance_criteria: Canary rollout to 10% of GPUs with runtime flag enabled and no manual intervention for 48h
95th percentile latency reduced >= 15% and 99th percentile reduced >= 10% on benchmark high-QPS trace vs baseline
OOM/eviction events reduced >= 25% on internal replay of problematic production traces
Telemetry with per-GPU thresholds, hold-delay histogram, KV preemption counts, and quality regression alerting in place
Config knob to switch between soft-delay and hard-shed modes plus automated revert rule implemented
